title: A thermodynamically favoured molecular computer.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Zenodo record 15869378 (MIT licence) holds one 290,124,440-byte zip (about 1.99 GB uncompressed, 1,917 entries). Over the 50 MB cap, so I read its zip index and pulled single small files with ranged requests. Contents: 229 raw qPCR (quantitative PCR fluorescence) .eds files, liquid-handler picklists, DNA strand sequence CSVs, code, and experiments_database.xlsx. That spreadsheet has 299 rows x 15 columns. expected_output is 1 in 152 rows, 0 in 117, 2 in 4 and missing in 26; 155 rows are computation wells and 92 are controls, across 11 programs (BITCOPY 46 rows, SIRM 40, R110 40, ... REACH 8). I also read the authors' binary_classifier.py, which fits a single threshold on completion_level.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The claims about 10 programs, 100-bit addition, reuse and sub-minute runs come from the abstract. I did not parse the .eds fluorescence time series.

a1_downloadable.note: Open Zenodo zip, MIT licence, no login; 290 MB, so I sampled it by ranged requests rather than downloading it whole (checked).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: expected_output (the designed correct bit, 0/1) is a column in experiments_database.xlsx, next to the measured completion_level (checked).

a3_inputs_present.note: Strand sequences are present in CSVs, and the raw fluorescence is in .eds files that need the qslib reader (checked file presence, not parsed).

a4_units_stated.note: completion_level is a normalised 0-1 fluorescence fraction; concentrations are in nM in the sequence CSVs (checked headers).

a5_enough_rows.note: 299 rows in the experiments table: about 155 computation wells plus 92 controls with a 0/1 label, spread over 11 programs. That is far under 400, even for classification (checked).

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~2 GB uncompressed total; the label table is 64 KB
a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially laptop-sized if only the summary table is used.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The 11 computation names in the table broadly match the 10 programs in the abstract plus controls; the per-program well counts weren't cross-checked against the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: The label is the designed answer to the computation, and the authors already separate it from the measured completion_level with one threshold. Learning the label from features would only rediscover a known threshold rule, not biology.

backbone.name: none applicable (synthetic DNA strands; nucleotide language models are trained on genomes, not on designed computing strands)

integration.join_key: none (strand names local to this paper)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: No joinable partner resource; the strands are synthetic designs with no standard identifiers.

controls.negative_control: Quench-only and buffer wells in the table.
controls.external_validation: None; one lab, one qPCR instrument.

honest_claim_h3: At best, the model would show that a single fluorescence threshold separates correct 0 and 1 outputs in about 270 wells from one lab, which the authors already did.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use fluorescence curves from DNA-computer wells to predict whether each well computed a 0 or 1 output bit.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-well fluorescence readouts and design metadata. The summary table has 299 wells, about 270 of them labelled.
plain_idea.predict: The expected output bit, which was set by the experimental design and read out by a fluorescent reporter on a qPCR machine.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Little: the authors already separate the two outputs with one threshold, and the dataset is too small and too synthetic to teach anything about biology.

label_elsewhere.sources: None; the outputs are specific to this paper's DNA programs.
label_elsewhere.why: No external labelled data exists for these designed strands.

ml_idea: Classify the output bit of each DNA-computer well from its qPCR fluorescence trace. Rejected: about 270 labelled wells, and a one-threshold rule already solves it.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from file sizes in the zip index; nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count labelled rows in experiments_database.xlsx: 299 rows, about 270 labelled. Done; it kills the project.

verdict_reason: Fails A5: only 299 wells (about 270 labelled) across 11 programs. Fails A8: the label is the designed output bit, which the authors already separate with a single threshold on measured completion. This is DNA nanotechnology, not a biological measurement set, and it has no backbone or join partner.
